def: An empirical power-law relationship between a model's loss and its parameters, training data or compute, which lets small runs predict larger ones.
A relationship y = a x^b, which is a straight line on log-log axes and changes y by a fixed factor for each fixed factor in x.
The part of the loss that no model size or data amount can remove, set by the entropy of the data itself.
The model size and token count that give the lowest loss for a fixed training compute budget.
DeepMind's 70-billion-parameter model trained on 1.4 trillion tokens, which outperformed the larger Gopher at equal compute and showed that size and data should grow together.
The ratio of training tokens to parameters, about 20 at the compute-optimal point in the Chinchilla analysis and far higher in models built for cheap serving.
The loss of models of different sizes that all use the same training compute, with a minimum at the compute-optimal size.
The model L(N, D) = E + A/N^a + B/D^b fitted to training runs, with an irreducible term, a capacity term and a data term.
Training a model on more tokens than the compute-optimal amount, accepting inefficient training in return for a smaller and cheaper model to serve.
Abilities that seem to appear abruptly at some model scale, whose sharpness is partly disputed as an effect of all-or-nothing metrics.
